segments: [Header:] ... year {OCR?}
of the Greeks (231 of our Lord?).
Ardashir son of Pabag (Babak?) became king over the Persians,
and the last kingdom of the Persians began, which is called that of the House of Sasan.
And the duration of the years was four hundred and eighteen,
until the kingdom of the Arabs arose and brought it to an end.
After [Alexander], [Maximinus] Caesar [ruled] three years {OCR?}.
This man, through hatred toward the one who was before him,
stirred up persecution against the Christians.
And Sergius and Bacchus, those who were sent to Mesopotamia, were martyred and crowned;
and also Cyprian the bishop and many others,
until that Maximinus was killed in Aquileia {OCR?}.
After Maximinus Caesar, Gordian [was] Caesar [and] ruled six years.
And he was killed on the borders of Persia.
In his days Mani was born. [Philip] Caesar [ruled] seven years {OCR?}.
In his time the persecution of Christians ceased.
And in his first year,
Shapur son of Ardashir became king over the Persians for thirty-one years.
And in his time was completed,
for the building of Rome,
a thousand years.
And wild beasts were killed in the Great Circus,
when the contest of the thousand years was celebrated;
and there were spectacles of Ares during the nights;
for three days there was a vigil,
and forty athletics [games],
as at the birthday festival of Rome,
were run.
And the Theatre of Pompey and the Hekatostylon,
that is, the [colonnade of] a hundred columns,
burned.
Philip himself, however, its lord, was killed by Decius. Decius was Caesar [and] ruled one year {OCR?}.
This man greatly persecuted the Christians.
And in his time the Seven Youths fled from Ephesus and hid themselves in a cave.
And many apostatized through fear of him.
And when he was killed and the wrath subsided,
those who had apostatized came to Rome
and asked for repentance.
And Novatus said
that there is no forgiveness;
and he was called the head of the Cathari.
[After Decius, Gallus and Volu]sianus were Caesars for two years {OCR?}.
And they were killed in the street of Flaminius.
At this time a destructive pestilence raged throughout the inhabited earth.
Novatus, the priest of Africa,
and Novatian, the priest of Rome:
the Holy Church anathematized this erroneous doctrine.
